bug_semantics: Client-side heap OOB write in smb2_add_iovector(): it stores into v->iov[v->niov] and increments niov with no upper bound against the fixed array iov[SMB2_MAX_VECTORS] (256). On receive, a compound SMB2 response with NextCommand set keeps the same smb2->in vector set, appending header/fixed/variable/pad iovecs for each chained PDU and then, when is_chained, adding another header and looping via goto read_more_data without resetting niov. A malicious server can therefore drive niov past 256 and write adjacent heap. SMB2_OPLOCK_BREAK notifications with message_id 0xffffffffffffffff skip smb2_find_pdu(), so the chain need not match outstanding request IDs; that is an exploitability amplifier, not the overflow sink. Unauthenticated remote DoS / potential RCE against a libsmb2 client.
flaw_origin: The complete CVE mechanism first appears in 189e5edab3ae792fc3d6d6a414d7166b57a269c6 (Ronnie Sahlberg, 2017-04-07), which reworked the receive state machine to handle SMB2 command chaining. That commit first wrote the is_chained = hdr.next_command path that smb2_add_iovector()s the next header onto smb2->in and continues without freeing the vector set. Immediate parent 984d7ede77e003ac1692f18318f6e17cdc81e1e0 has no next_command/is_chained receive loop (single PDU, then reset). smb2_add_iovector() itself was already an unbounded helper (a3173ff90979760d03bf473e3f0982d7cfdef049) and SMB2_MAX_VECTORS was already 256 (fcad57cb9378f81c7b22dd5d0f131983f9cfdb80); those earlier commits do not implement the chained-PDU accumulation the advisory describes. Later OPLOCK_BREAK message-id bypass (b98e4972 / ebb60e9b) only widened triggerability.

Advisory/gist mechanism: chained SMB2 NextCommand repeatedly calls smb2_add_iovector() without checking v->niov vs SMB2_MAX_VECTORS=256; OPLOCK_BREAK bypasses message-id validation. First-party gist https://gist.github.com/ZjW1nd/0b95b63307ceee7890e88e4abc6f041e points at include/libsmb2-private.h, lib/init.c, lib/socket.c and PR https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2/pull/431.

reasoning: CVE-2025-57632 is a published, non-withdrawn heap overflow: smb2_add_iovector() appends to a 256-slot iovec array with no niov cap, and the SMB2 receive path keeps appending across NextCommand-chained PDUs on one smb2->in object, so a malicious server can walk niov off the heap. The OPLOCK_BREAK path that skips message-id matching only makes unbounded chaining easier; the cited fix does not change that path. The smallest public commit that first wrote this chained-receive mechanism is 189e5edab3ae792fc3d6d6a414d7166b57a269c6. Its parent 984d7ede lacks NextCommand looping (verified on the parent tree), so the overflow-via-chain is absent immediately before the BIC. Earlier unbounded smb2_add_iovector (a3173ff) and the MAX_VECTORS=256 bump (fcad57cb) are prerequisites, not the first write of the CVE trigger; blaming those would invert the advisory's chained-PDU mechanism. 189e5ed is a single-parent non-merge commit with no reconstructable member commits.
